name: Central Bai
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Allen, Bryan. 2007. Bai Dialect Survey (SIL, incl. Jianchuan/Central Bai phonologies); also Wiersma, Grace. 2003. Yunnan Bai, in The Sino-Tibetan Languages. sil.org could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Zhang Jinlin 张锦琳. 2026. 云龙白语四音格词语音特征研究 [A study of the phonetic features of quadrisyllabic compound words in Yunlong Bai]. 现代语言学 Modern Linguistics 14(1): 193-202. doi:10.12677/ml.2026.141026
sources.note: Yunlong county variety (Central Bai area per Allen 2007 coding). Discusses reduplication patterns and 'rhythm/韵律和谐' of four-syllable elaborate expressions only; no word-stress or 重音/轻声 statement.

sources.citation: StressTyp2 (2015 archive), WALS (Goedemans & van der Hulst ch. 14-17; Maddieson 13A), LAPSyD - database checks
sources.note: StressTyp2 has no Bai record (only the Ethnologue code row 'bca Bai, Central'); WALS codes Bai only for 13A tone = 'complex tone system' (source Dell 1981) and has no 14A-17A stress values; LAPSyD (lapsyd.huma-num.fr) has no Bai entry.

sources.citation: Wiersma, Grace. 2003. Yunnan Bai. In Graham Thurgood & Randy J. LaPolla (eds.), The Sino-Tibetan Languages, 651-673. London: Routledge. (sec. 2 Phonology, pp. 654-657, Jianchuan dialect)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number PL3521.S56 2017); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.note: Nothing. Describes syllable canon and an 8-tone system with modal/non-modal phonation; 'Syllables in the Bai language are invariably open and every syllable is considered to be tone-bearing.' No mention of stress, accent, unstressed or reduced syllables anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A., John H. Esling & Li Shaoni. 2021 [online 27 Apr 2020]. Jianchuan Bai (Illustrations of the IPA). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 51(3): 490-501. doi:10.1017/S0025100319000379
sources.note: No statement on word stress. Sections: Consonants, Vowels, Tonal register (55, 33, 31, 21, 35 x lax/tense registers), Conventions, narrative passage. Only prosody-adjacent remark: 'A reduced [ə] occurs morphophonemically in the second syllable of words where that syllable bears a particle relationship to the first syllable' (Conventions). Speaker from Qiaohou, Jianchuan region (glottocode jian1239 cited).

sources.citation: Benner, Allison & John H. Esling. 2014. Acoustic cues to tone and register in Bai: adult baseline data. Proceedings of Speech Prosody 2014. doi:10.21437/speechprosody.2014-121
sources.note: Nothing; acoustic study of the 15-way tone x register paradigm on monosyllables.

sources.citation: Lee, Yeon-Ju & Laurent Sagart. 2008. No limits to borrowing: the case of Bai and Chinese. Diachronica 25(3): 357-385. (HAL hal-00781005)
sources.note: Nothing. Brief outline of Jianchuan Bai phonology (syllable C(G)V(G), initials, tones, from Huang et al. 1992 TBL pp. 675-676 and Xu & Zhao 1984); loanword strata study.

sources.citation: Allen, Bryan (艾磊). 2007. Bai Dialect Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2007-012. 124 pp. (= Allen & Zhang Xia 2004, 白语方言研究 Baiyu fangyan yanjiu, Kunming: Yunnan Minzu Chubanshe)
sources.note: Named by the earlier scan; contains phonological sketches/wordlists for Jianchuan, Heqing, Lanping, Yunlong, Eryuan (all Central Bai). Open PDF exists but the sil.org /system/files path is an automated-access block-challenged by automated download and the the Internet Archive was offline.

sources.citation: Wang, Feng. 2006. Comparison of Languages in Contact: The Distillation Method and the Case of Bai. Language and Linguistics Monograph Series B, Frontiers in Linguistics III. Taipei: Institute of Linguistics, Academia Sinica. 260 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (no hits for stress, accent, 重音). Gives Bai syllable structure (C)(S)V(C) (Table 10, p. 32), tone inventories of nine dialects and a tone-sandhi rule; Jianchuan data cited from Xu & Zhao 1984.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. & Li Shaoni. 1994. Voice quality and voice quality change in the Bai language of Yunnan Province. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 17(2): 49-68.
sources.note: Instrumental study of Jianchuan Bai phonation (modal/breathy/tense/harsh) and four pitch trajectories; introduction (pp. 49-53, scanned) contains no word-stress statement. Remaining pages are acoustic results (not scanned).

sources.citation: Dell, François. 1981. La langue bai: phonologie et lexique [book notice]. Cahiers de Linguistique Asie Orientale 10: 143. (Persée clao_0153-3320_1981_num_10_1_1248)
sources.note: One-page notice of the monograph; establishes that Dell 1981's phonological description is of 'le parler bai de Da-li' (Dali = Southern Bai), not Jianchuan. Nothing on accent. The PDF itself is captcha-gated; page text.

sources.citation: Xu Lin 徐琳 & Zhao Yansun 赵衍荪. 1984. 白语简志 (Baiyu jianzhi) [A brief description of the Bai language]. 中国少数民族语言简志丛书. Beijing: Minzu Chubanshe. 179 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The standard primary description of Jianchuan (Central) Bai; its 语音 chapter (声母/韵母/声调/音节, 语流音变) is the most likely place for an explicit 重音/轻声 statement and is the source all later English works rely on. HathiTrust mdp.39015051448168 (search-only).

sources.citation: Zhao Yanzhen 赵燕珍 (with Dai Qingxia). 2012. 赵庄白语参考语法 [Reference grammar of Zhaozhuang Bai]. Beijing: Zhongguo Shehui Kexue Chubanshe. 303 pp. ISBN 9787516101483.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only full modern reference grammar of a Bai variety (参考语法 series volumes normally have an explicit 音节/韵律/重音 subsection). NB Glottolog codes Zhaozhuang as Southern Bai [bfs], so it would be a proxy, not Central Bai proper.

sources.citation: Li Shaoni 李绍尼 & Jerold A. Edmondson (艾杰瑞). 1990. 云南剑川白语音质和音调类型 (Yunnan Jianchuan Baiyu yinzhi he yindiao leixing) [Phonetic quality and tone types of Jianchuan Bai, Yunnan]. 中央民族学院学报 1990(5). (record seen in Wang Feng 2006 bibliography and Glottolog)

sources.note: Chinese-language phonetic/phonological study specifically of Jianchuan Bai suprasegmentals; may contain remarks on 轻重音 absent from the English instrumental papers.

sources.note: Fullest English-language description of Jianchuan Bai (Glottolog type: grammar); the 2003 chapter is a 'much-reduced version'. A phonology chapter of this length is likely to state whether Bai has word stress / how disyllables are realised.
